preRules.note: A virama that ends a word (before a space, punctuation, a danda, a digit, or at the end of the text) is the visible halant: written as ્+ZWNJ, as the composer writes that. Every Unicode font draws it so; the half form the composer answers for a bare virama is only what it shows while it waits for the next letter.

A virama with no letter before it, before ન: the composer writes ્ન alone as ન 5F (U+FDD3 marks it for that pair). After a letter the virama is the letter's own (જ્ઞ્ન = 6F B9 5F, as જ્ઞ્મ = 6F B9 64), never dropped.

Reph: ર્ before a letter is written after that letter and its signs (U+FDD0 marks it for the pairs) - and before the halant of a virama that ends the word (આર્ત્ = 41 70 73 AE B9: the reph on ત, not on આ). Before ર the composer writes ર and the ra-sign instead.
A cluster ending in ya with no sign after it (or with the halant of a word-final virama): the full letter and the ya-sign E9 (U+FDD2 marks it for the pairs).
Move pre-base matra U+0ABF before the consonant cluster (Unicode logical order -> legacy visual order).
Nukta: written before its letter (and before a conjunct it ends).

postRules.note: Va after ઙ છ ટ ઠ ડ ઢ દ: the va-sign 99 after the spacer.
u after ફ હ દ્ર ફ્ર હ્ર: BA.
uu after ફ હ દ્ર ફ્ર હ્ર: 9F.
Ra-sign after a letter with a spacer: B2, before the spacer.
Ra-sign under ળ: B2.
Signs above and below a letter go before its spacer.
છ જ દ: only the signs below go before the spacer.
The halant goes before its letter's spacer, as the composer writes ક્‌ = 4C B9 24 - after a reph too (ર્ક્ ending a word = 4C AE B9 24); a tall letter keeps its signs above after the spacer.
Ra-sign + u: one glyph.
Ra-sign + uu: one glyph.
e + anusvara: one glyph.
ai + anusvara: one glyph.
ii + anusvara: one glyph.
i-sign: the wide glyph 72 except before ક ઙ ટ ઠ ડ ઢ દ ફ ર.
i-sign + anusvara over one letter: 74.
i-sign over a cluster: the long glyph 5B.
e + reph: one glyph.
ai + reph: one glyph.
ii + reph: one glyph.
ii + anusvara + reph: one glyph.
e + anusvara + reph: one glyph.
ai + anusvara + reph: one glyph.
anusvara + reph: one glyph.

P3b (round 2): a vocalic-l sign the fonts have no glyph for passes through as itself, and Word draws it in a fallback font on a dotted circle of its own - a reph written after it (as the composer writes ર્કૢ: 4C 24 AE, the reph after the spacer) sat on that circle. The reph goes first, on its letter: ર્કૢ = 4C 24 AE U+0AE2, the composer's bytes and the sign after them.
4/5/6: ઙ્ક standing whole is the one code 91.
4/5/6: ઙ્ક્ષ standing whole is the one code B6.
4/5/6: ઙ્ખ standing whole is the one code 92.
4/5/6: ઙ્ગ standing whole is the one code 93.
4/5/6: ઙ્ઘ standing whole is the one code 94.
U+FDD1 in a pair keeps the rules above off a spelling the composer writes its own way; it is not text.
